charts.title: The dead-shoot objection as a simulation.
charts.takeaway: With the room drift we assumed, a lever on a dead shoot reads 5.2 micrometres an hour against a true growth of 2.0; subtracting a paired dead shoot recovers the mean (2.04) with a spread of 1.03.
charts.n: 300 simulated lever runs with assumed drift ranges; no plant was measured

steps.label: Planted: growth of 2.0 micrometres an hour
steps.detail: A live shoot that grows at a known rate and a dead shoot that does not grow, on the same lever, in a room that warms and dampens by amounts we assumed.

steps.label: What the lever reads
steps.detail: The live shoot reads a mean of 7.2; the dead shoot reads 5.2, and 94 percent of dead runs read above 1.

steps.label: Control: a paired dead shoot
steps.detail: Subtracting the dead shoot's reading gives a mean of 2.04 with a spread of 1.03; 67 percent of single runs land within 1 of the truth.

steps.label: The reading restates the assumed drift
steps.detail: The dead-shoot number follows from the drift ranges by arithmetic. It shows the size of drift that would bury the growth and is no evidence about the historical instrument.

charts.title: False alarms on stems that never stop growing, by scenario and detector.
charts.takeaway: Neither detector raises a false alarm on data made by its own model. Under misfit at 5 micrometres a day they alarm on 62 and 46 percent of stems that are still growing.
charts.units: percent of 200 simulated stems that never stop growing on which the detector flagged a stop
charts.n: 200 stopping and 200 non-stopping simulated stems in each of five scenarios; one seed
charts.no_interval: The study computed no interval; each share rests on 200 simulated stems from one seed.
charts.baseline: The matched scenarios, where the simulated stem follows the detector's own model
charts.threshold: No bar was set in advance for the misfit scenarios, which were added after the matched result was seen

axis.label: false alarms on stems that never stop (percent)
